name: Laicism
summary: Laicism (laïcité) is the principle that the State is autonomous of religious authority and neutral between religions and convictions. It rests on freedom of conscience, the autonomy of politics from particular religious norms, and non-discrimination. It does not abolish religion; the French 1905 law recognises, pays and subsidises no cult while guaranteeing worship.
scope: Laicism as defined in the 2005 Universal Declaration on Laicity of the 21st Century, with the French 1905 separation law and current French public-service rules as the state record. It does not cover Turkish Kemalist laicism or militant anticlerical state atheism, and answers only church-state questions that these texts settle.
